passage:
Coach's note, Sunday. Noor writing about Imran, who came to our community finance desk after a difficult tax matter.
The matter had been settled, but Imran's records had been a mess: small freelance payments in phone messages, receipts in a shoebox. Since then, Imran has changed how things work. On the first Sunday of each month, Imran turns up with a sealed envelope of receipts and screenshots and enters each one in a plain sheet with a column for side income.
I did not tell Imran what to record; I only asked what next year's filing would need. Imran said, "Fewer mismatches, and no scramble." Today the sheet matched the bank statement line by line, and Imran's shoulders eased.
— Noor

qa.q: On which day of the month does Imran bring the envelope?
qa.a: Imran brings it on the first Sunday of each month.

qa.q: What was Imran probably feeling when the sheet matched the bank statement?
qa.a: Imran was probably relieved and a bit proud, shown by the shoulders easing after a messy year.

qa.q: What could Imran do if a payment has no receipt?
qa.a: Imran could write it in the sheet the same day with the date, amount and payer, and ask the payer for a note if possible.

qa.q: What is it like for Noor to watch Imran's new routine?
qa.a: Noor is encouraged and glad, seeing the routine grow by Imran's own choice and only asking questions about it.

grounding: The note shows a person, after settling a tax matter, tracking side income and receipts monthly so that the next filing has complete records.

Sunday, 3 November
New system, day one. After four months of that notice, I am never again rebuilding a year of side income from old chat messages.
What I set up today:
1. A spreadsheet called 'Side income', one row per payment: date, who paid, amount, what for.
2. A folder where every receipt goes, named by month.
3. A calendar alert on the 1st of each month: 'Update side income. 15 minutes.'
Afreen, who's been freelancing longer than me, does hers every Sunday, but monthly is enough for my four or five clients.
Filled in October already: three illustration jobs, one workshop. Took twelve minutes. I actually feel lighter. Next July, at filing time, it's just a total to copy, not a detective story.
Charu

qa.q: What does the calendar alert say?
How does Charu feel after filling in October?
qa.a: Charu feels lighter and relieved, knowing next July's filing will be a total to copy, not a detective story.

qa.q: What else could Charu add to make the next filing smoother?
qa.a: Charu could ask a chartered accountant once which records the return needs, so the spreadsheet tracks exactly those.

qa.q: How might Afreen see Charu's new system?
qa.a: Afreen, who updates every Sunday, may be pleased to see a friend take up a habit that suits a smaller client list.

grounding: It shows a person who, after a tax notice, starts tracking side income and receipts every month so the next filing has complete records.

Aparna: so is the notice thing finally over?
Disha: closed! officer accepted the reply 🎉
Aparna: party?
Disha: no. admin. sending you a photo
Disha: [photo of a box file labelled RENT 2024-25]
Aparna: is that... a box file. who are you
Disha: every month from now: rent receipt from the tenant, society bill, any repair bill. all in here, and scanned to a folder
Aparna: every month??
Disha: 1st of every month, 10 mins. the notice happened because I forgot two months of rent when I filed. never again
Aparna: honestly smart. can you do mine
Disha: no 😅 buy your own box file
Aparna: fine. send me the photo again, I'm copying the label

qa.q: What goes in the box file every month?
qa.a: The rent receipt from the tenant, the society bill and any repair bill.

qa.q: How is Disha feeling now that the notice is closed?
qa.a: Disha is relieved and pleased 🎉 but also determined, choosing a new habit over a party.

qa.q: What else could Disha try so the monthly habit sticks?
qa.a: Disha could set a phone reminder for the 1st and back up the scanned folder, so the habit doesn't rely on memory.

qa.q: How does Disha's new habit look to Aparna?
qa.a: Aparna teases at first, then thinks it's smart enough to copy the label for Aparna's own box file.

grounding: It shows a person revising record-keeping after a notice, collecting rent and repair receipts monthly so the next filing is complete.
